subject: Vietnam
note: Hand-curated from the pinned World Bank series (public/geo/series.json): GDP per capita, current US$ (NY.GDP.PCAP.CD), 1990 and 2022. Current dollars are not adjusted for inflation, so every country's figure rises; the claim compares growth between countries. Counts use the 190 countries and territories with a figure in both years.

claims.text: Vietnam's GDP per capita (current US$) was US$98.80 in 1990 and US$4,147.69 in 2022, about 42 times as much.
China's GDP per capita (current US$) was US$318.50 in 1990 and US$12,970.61 in 2022, about 41 times as much.
Among the 190 countries and territories with figures in both years, Vietnam had the largest multiple, followed by China.
41 of those 190 had a GDP per capita of US$10,000 or more in 1990, and 81 in 2022 (current US$).
The figures are in current US dollars and are not adjusted for inflation.
